{{nihongo|'''Taga Shrine'''|多賀神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mutsu Province]].

[[ja:多賀神社 (宮城県名取郡)]]

{{wikidata link|Q11431092|ja|多賀神社 (宮城県名取郡)|check_date=2026-05-26}}

== Japanese content ==

'''Taga Shrine'' (Taga Shrine) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Miyagi Prefecture|Q47896|qid=Q47896}} former {{ill|Natori District, Miyagi|Q6980219|qid=Q6980219}}.
{{ill|Mutsu Province|Q907389|qid=Q907389}}{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki}}{{ill|Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikiuchi Shrine}} Among the 100 shrines, one of the two in {{ill|Natori District, Miyagi|Q6980219|qid=Q6980219}} The two shrines currently enshrined in Tomizawa and {{ill|Natori, Miyagi|Q642018|qid=Q642018}} Takayanagi are considered to be Ronsha.

=== Enshrined God ===
* {{ill|Izanagi|Q813858|qid=Q813858|lt=Izanagison}} is enshrined as the main deity.
* In addition, {{ill|Kasuga Shrines|Q10855011|qid=Q10855011}} (enshrined deity: {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|UNKNOWN|Ame-no-Koyane|lt=Amagiya-no-Mikoto}}) and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Takarayu Shrine}} (enshrined deity: {{ill|Kuraokami|Q644201|qid=Q644201|lt=Takaranokami}}) are also enshrined together.

===Venue===
The area where Taga Shrine is located is also a historically important area, as there are Jomon period ruins such as Tomizawa Ruins and Onoda Ruins, the Onoda Tumulus Group, and {{ill|Sendai Kōriyama Kanga ruins|Q11643209|qid=Q11643209}}.

Taga Shrine is ``the oldest shrine in Sendai City,'' and according to the shrine's legend, it was prayed to by {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nihon Takeru}} during his conquest of Toi in the 40th year of Emperor Keiko (110). It is said that in the 21st {{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|Q357235|qid=Q357235}} 2nd year ({{ill|458|Q30922|qid=Q30922}}), he was given 58 bundles of Keida and held a divine ritual ceremony. It is said that in ancient times it was called ``Otakanomiya''.

According to the precinct history book, Taga Shrine was deeply revered by feudal lords and military commanders as the guardian deity of this region. It is said that during the reign of the 70th Emperor Go-Reizei, {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshiie|Q32613|qid=Q32613}}, the shogun of the military base, crossed the {{ill|Natori River|Q11414763|qid=Q11414763}} and worshiped at the shrine during his eastern expedition, praying for good fortune and long life and dedicating something in his own handwriting.

The temporary shrine built during {{ill|Kyōhō|Q1145048|qid=Q1145048}} was severely damaged. Afterwards, it was revered by successive lords of the Sendai domain, and the construction of the shrine building was carried out in {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yasunaga}}4 ({{ill|1775|Q7700|qid=Q7700}}) with a donation from {{ill|Date Shigemura|Q846378|qid=Q846378}}. It is said that the lord of Kakuda Castle, {{ill|Ishikawa Munemitsu|Q11585764|qid=Q11585764}}, presented the shrine with the divine name ``Taga Shrine Izanagison,'' and the shrine was crowded with visitors from his wives and maids.{{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} It was designated as a village shrine in April 1950, and in 1942 it was enshrined together with Kasuga Shrine in the Onoda district and Horyu Shrine in the Noda district of Higashidai, and in August 1988 it was designated as a Heihaku Kushinsha.

===Enshrined God===
*{{ill|Izanagi|Q813858|qid=Q813858|lt=Izanamison}} and {{ill|Izanami|Q682306|qid=Q682306|lt=Izanamison}} are enshrined as the main deities.
*In addition, the shrine enshrines the deities of nearby shrines, such as Kumano Kaoro Kushimokukunokami, {{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Omikami}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Hasusao no Mikoto}}, and {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997}}.

===Venue===
It is said that he was solicited by Takeru Takeru of Japan in February 28th year of Emperor Keiko's expedition to the east. It is said that in November of the second year of Emperor Yuryaku's reign (458), a festival was held in which 58 bundles of Keida were offered as a ritual field. To the east of our company, there is a place called ``Keida'', which is named after the ritual field that was given to us at that time.

According to the history of the shrine, when Takeru Takeru of Japan came to Oshu to conquer the east, he suffered from a serious illness due to a series of battles and long journeys. At that time, he set up an altar and a shrine in a warm area where willows grew and prayed for his recovery, and it is said that he recovered and was able to return safely to the land of Yamato. It is said that the shrine where people prayed for recovery from illness and peace of the nation was the origin of Taga Shrine.

The area where our company is located still bears the name of the area associated with this history.
*To the north of Taga Shrine is Kodangahara, the place where Takeru Nihon built an altar to pray for victory in battle.
*``Tanayanagi'' (Tanayanagi → Takayanagi) (current name of the enshrined place) is the place where an altar was made from a willow tree and people prayed for recovery from illness.

Additionally, Shiratori Shrine, which enshrines the spirit of Japan Takeru, is located on the premises of a private house 970 meters southeast of our company.
<gallery widths="200px" heights="150px">
File:Precincts of Shiratori-jinja shrine in Natori city.JPG|Precincts of Shiratori-jinja shrine
File:Shiratori-jinja shrine at Natori city.JPG|Shiratori-jinja shrineFile:Honden of Shiratori-jinja shrine in Natori city.JPG|Honden of Shiratori-jinja shrine
</gallery>

It is said that there have been frequent disputes between our company and Taga Shrine in Tomizawa, Taihaku Ward, Sendai City over which shrine is the Shikinai Shrine, Taka Shrine. The history book ``Shinsen Mutsu Fudoki'' states that ``Taga Shrine was originally located in Tomizawa Village, but is now enshrined in Takayanagi Village.'' However, Taga Shrine in Takayanagi was originally called ``Wakamiya Hachiman,'' but it was renamed Taga Shrine.'' A controversy arose in 1897, which led to the conclusion that Taga Shrine in Tomizawa was Shikinai shrine, and Taga Shrine in Takayanagi was the land where the shrine's territory, such as ritual fields, was located. The place name ``''{{ill|Nishitaga|Q11627540|qid=Q11627540|lt=Nishitaga}}''' in Taihaku Ward is derived from Taga Shrine in Tomizawa, and the area around our company in Yuriage district and Takayanagi was previously called ``''{{ill|Yuriage|Q11655485|qid=Q11655485|lt=Higashitaga}}'''.

It became a local shrine in February 1894, and was later designated as a Heihaku Kushinsha. He was respected by the lord of the domain and the governor of Mutsu Province. In connection with the history of Nihon Takeru, the shrine attracts many worshipers not only from nearby areas but also from other prefectures as a shrine that is particularly blessed with healing from illness and extending life.

===Precincts===
*Shrine building (Haden of worship, Heiden, Nagaruzo main building)
*There is a shrine gate and a shrine office within the precincts.
